Find numeric values far from what other datasets report for the same genus

Source: R/dataset_checks.R
dataset_check_outlier_by_genus.Rd

As dataset_check_outlier_by_species(), but compares each value with the values other datasets report for any taxon in the same genus, as given by the genus column of the database's taxa table. Use it for taxa that too few other datasets have measured for the species-level check, bearing in mind that species within a genus can legitimately differ by far more than individuals within a species: a genus of herbs and trees will flag every tree. Taxa without a genus, such as names resolved only to family, are not checked.

dataset_check_outlier_by_genus(
  database,
  dataset_ids = NULL,
  trait_names = NULL,
  min_fold = 100,
  min_other_datasets = 2,
  value_types = list(central = c("mean", "median", "mode", "raw"), minimum = "minimum",
    maximum = "maximum")
)

Arguments

database

Compiled database object, e.g. austraits

dataset_ids

dataset_id's to check. The default, NULL, checks every dataset in the database against the rest.

trait_names

Traits to check. The default, NULL, checks every numeric trait that cannot be negative.

min_fold

Values that differ from other_median by at least this factor, in either direction, are listed in records. The default, 100, is higher than for species: in a sample from AusTraits, values 30- to 100-fold from the rest of their genus were often species that genuinely differ, while most beyond 100-fold were errors.

min_other_datasets

Minimum number of other datasets with values for the taxon and trait for a value to be compared. The default, 2, means a value is only flagged when it disagrees with the consensus of at least two other datasets, rather than with a single one that might be the one in error. Set it to 1 to also check taxa only one other dataset has measured.

value_types

List of groups of value_types to compare with each other; see Details. A value whose value_type is in no group is not checked.

Value

As dataset_check_outlier_by_species(), with genus and n_other_taxa added to records.

Details

other_median is the median, across every taxon in the genus and every other dataset, of the median of each taxon's values in each dataset, so each taxon a dataset measured counts once. n_other_taxa is the number of taxa those values come from.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dataset_check_outlier_by_genus(austraits, "Ooi_2007")$records
} # }
